output.title: Where churn signals actually begin
output.body:
Churn signals usually do not start as a dashboard problem. They start with one owner noticing the same customers going quiet, buying less often, or changing the tone of their messages before they stop repeating. The useful question is not “can AI predict churn?” It is: do you already have a repeatable trail of events before a customer lapses?

For a 1–10 person business, I would separate two kinds of signal. First is gut feel: “sales feel softer this month.” That is worth hearing, but it is not yet a workflow. Second is pattern-based: “these behaviours show up before a cancellation.” That is the version you can check, document, and eventually automate. AI only helps with the second one, and only if the relevant data already exists in your email, CRM notes, order history, or support messages.

If the trail is there, the next step is simple and non-technical: review one month of cancellations or lapses and list the last visible touchpoints, complaints, delays, or silence before each one. Then ask which of those signals appears most often. That gives you a bounded pilot scope. If the trail is not there, no model is going to rescue the missing paper trail. Annoying, but tidy.

The owner still makes the decision; the software only follows the record.
